# Once v0.3.0

Changes since v0.2.1, grouped by platform.

## Upgrade note

This release moves story-source settings to a versioned, typed document. Source
configuration migrates only after the initial settings sync completes. Update
every client that shares the database before editing sources: mixed v0.2.x and
v0.3.0 source editing is unsupported, and an old-client change after cutover is
reported as a split configuration instead of being merged.

## Across all platforms

- **Durable story-source identity.** Sources and groups now have stable ids that
  survive URL edits, renames, reordering and duplicate insertion. Empty groups,
  duplicate group names and duplicate URLs remain representable.
- **Structured source configuration.** The Sources editor works from typed
  objects and offers URL, label, collector, enabled and group fields. Its text
  view uses deterministic JSON, validates the whole edit before saving, and
  keeps search, error navigation and highlighting attached to the correct
  source.
- **Safer configurable collectors.** Collector ids are stable persistence
  identifiers, selector configuration is normalized at the collector boundary,
  and the picker previews and saves source objects without rebuilding legacy
  encoded lines.
- **Sync-gated migration.** A configured client stays on its in-memory legacy
  sources while offline and does not write the new document until settings have
  replicated. Existing typed data wins over the legacy copy, and later legacy
  edits produce a visible diagnostic.
- Disabled sources are skipped completely and no longer contribute inactive
  groups or collector types to story filters.

## Electron (desktop) and extensions (Firefox & Chrome)

- Keyboard commands now follow the capabilities of each shell, including a
  story-reload command and browser-extension command forwarding that preserves
  normal text entry.
- The source editor, search results, error log and picker all use durable source
  ids across reloads and synchronization.

## Electron (desktop)

- Reader requests are tied to the tab that initiated them, preventing a late
  extraction or navigation error from being delivered to the wrong tab.
- Source-picker coverage now exercises the packaged typed-source flow, including
  editable configuration, cancellation and invalid-URL rejection.

## Mobile (Android & iOS)

- Source groups, ordering and picker output use the same typed document as the
  desktop and extension clients.

## Build and tests

- Added deterministic migration, normalization, collector-contract, settings,
  source-loading and cross-client synchronization coverage.
- Expanded Electron, Chrome, Firefox and mobile end-to-end coverage for typed
  source persistence and navigation.
- Corrected the macOS keyboard test expectation for shell-specific shortcuts.
